source: Create a subway surfer type of game called Neighborhood Woofer. The runner is Gloo, a light brown mini golden doodle. He is running through the streets with 3 lanes. There are incoming cars, garbage trucks, Karens who blocking the road, trash to jump over, obstables to duck under. He can pick up treats on the ground for different power ups like speed, invincibility. Track scores of distance traveled. If he trips 3 times, he will be captured by animal control. If he runs through the whole course, about 30s of running, he will reach his daddy (Andy), an asian guy with glasses.

answers.ask: Thirty seconds of running works out around 500 studs at walk speed — should the street be about that long, or longer as he speeds up?
answers.answer: Make the street about 500 studs long for the intended roughly 30-second run; keep the pace consistent rather than extending the course for speed boosts.

answers.ask: Once he reaches Andy, does the game end, or does the course loop and get harder?
answers.answer: Reaching Andy ends the run as a win.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D endless-runner-style neighborhood street course about 500 studs long, arranged as a straight three-lane road. Gloo, a light-brown mini goldendoodle, runs down the center of the scene through incoming cars, garbage trucks, pedestrians blocking lanes, ground trash, and low overhead obstacles, with dog treats placed along the road. Neighborhood buildings and sidewalks frame both sides of the street. At the far end of the course, Andy, an Asian man with glasses, waits as the finish-point figure.
blob:
## Genre
The genre is Infinite Runner: forward motion and three-lane reaction dodging define the play, even though this particular run has a finite endpoint.

## Shape and preset
Use `lane-snap`, a straight fixed-lane corridor with exactly three discrete choices across the street. The preset is Lane Runner, adapted from modular endless generation to one authored 500-stud course because the brief explicitly ends at Andy.

## Config requirements
Use `obstacle-moving` for incoming cars and garbage trucks crossing or occupying lanes, and `obstacle-jump` for road trash and low overhead barriers requiring jumps or ducks. `settlement-density` draws neighborhood buildings and sidewalks tightly framing both sides. `npc-population` draws the pedestrians obstructing lanes and Andy waiting visibly at the finish.

## Layout requirements
Place `collectible-nodes` as dog-treat trails along safe and riskier lane lines throughout the course, and place `powerup-buffs` among those treats for speed and invincibility pickups. The layout half of `npc-population` sites Andy at the center of the far-end finish area and distributes blocking pedestrians only where at least one valid lane remains. Add a finish trigger at Andy with no canonical option ID.

## Layout components
Build one straight road 500 studs long with three equal lanes, sidewalks and continuous neighborhood facades on both sides. Sequence incoming cars, garbage trucks, pedestrian blockers, trash piles, and duck-under obstacles without ever sealing all three lanes. The start occupies the near end; Andy and a clearly readable finish apron occupy the far end. Keep the long road centered in frame and preserve a clear forward sightline.

## Render order
Render `topdown` first and treat it as authoritative, because obstacle combinations and the three-lane safe route must remain playable from start to finish.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is large, driven by the stated 500-stud length. The theme is cheerful cartoon neighborhood adventure. Route through `P6` because every obstacle sequence must be valid by construction; no extra modifier is required.
